title: Latency-SLO-aware regional allocator with capacity S-curves
creator: Anjali Chopra
description: Design and implement a regional request allocator that honors per-customer latency SLOs while making routing decisions based on live capacity S-curves and geo-affinity. The allocator will calculate a Regional Affinity Score (RAS) per candidate region combining: observed p95/p99 latency headroom against SLO, real-time capacity utilization (GPU/CPU/KV cache), cost delta, and configurable geo soft-pinning weights. The goal is to reduce SLO violations during partial regional degradations without triggering mass failovers or unnecessary hedging that increases cost. This work ties into the runtime routing layer and the control plane's policy engine and will include a graceful circuit breaker that performs token-budgeted load shedding when headroom is exhausted.
discussion: 2025-11-10 - Kickoff: scoped to routing decision surface only, not placement changes at infra level. Action: prototype RAS calculator in python service (Luis).
2025-11-11 - PM feedback (Ravi): ensure explicit per-customer SLO overrides (enterprise customers may have tighter p99). Add feature flag for canary rollout.
2025-11-12 - Design review: DES suggested soft-pin UI for Console allowing fractional regional weights (e.g., 70% EU, 30% US). Follow-up: add Console API contract to attachments.

2025-11-13 - Eng discussion: trade-off between aggressive hedging and cost. Decided to prefer SLO preservation for p99 over cost for P0 customers; default policy will be cost-aware for P2/P3 customers.

2025-11-15 - Incident note: during ENG-9047 test scenario, naive hedging amplified downstream KV cache thrash. Decision: include KV cache hit-rate into capacity S-curve input and penalize regions with low prefix cache hit-rate.
2025-11-16 - Security: Security reviewed the policy for possibility of amplifying cross-region data flows; recommend throttles and audit logs. Security review required flag set.
2025-11-17 - Implementation update: initial Go implementation of ranking function ready. Added feature flag 'routing.v2.ras' and unit tests for RAS monotonicity.
decisions: Use a composite Regional Affinity Score (RAS) combining latency headroom, capacity S-curve percentile, geo-weight, and cost delta. RAS = w1*latency_score + w2*capacity_score + w3*geo_weight + w4*cost_penalty.
Adopt capacity S-curves rather than single-threshold checks: regions map utilization to an S-curve that penalizes high utilization more sharply near saturation to avoid cliff failovers.

Circuit breaker semantics will be hierarchical: node-level -> region-level -> global fallback. Region-level breaker trips when EWMA of request latency and resource utilization exceed thresholds for 1 minute.

Load shedding will be token-budgeted: requests carry a shedding budget that can be decremented on retries/hedges; budget exhaustion causes probabilistic shedding guided by customer priority and SLO class.
Enable per-customer SLO overrides and Console control for 'soft pin' fractional percentages. Default soft-pin is 1.0 for geographic customers (strict pinning) and 0.7 for general traffic.
Integrate KV cache hit-rate and tokenization cost into capacity_score to reflect real workload shape and cache pressure.
next_steps: Finish Go implementation of RAS ranking and add integration tests against the routing simulator (deadline 2025-11-22).
Wire ranking outputs to decision log stream (tracing + Console) for debugging and per-request attribution.
Implement region-level circuit breaker with EWMA thresholds and a 3-stage backoff policy (soft-shed -> redirect -> full-shed).
Create Console soft-pin UI mock and API contract; DES to produce final mocks by 2025-11-20.
Run chaos experiments in staging to validate graceful degradation and measure false-positive shedding rates (SRE + chaos team).
Prepare rollout plan: canary on 5% of tenants, monitor p99 error budget burn and cost delta. Rollback criteria defined in attachments.
